spatial_claims.claim: C is a point on segment AB, dividing it into segments AC and CB

configuration_map: The only geometric configuration is the given: a line segment AB with a point C on it, creating two sub-segments AC and CB. No auxiliary points, lines, angles, or figures are constructed. All rectangles and squares (rect(AB,AC), sq(AC), rect(AC,CB), etc.) are referenced purely as algebraic area quantities, never as geometric figures with spatial positions. The proof proceeds entirely through algebraic substitution using Propositions 2.2 and 2.3.
skip_reason: The AI proof is purely algebraic with no geometric configuration claims to check. Unlike Heath's proof, which constructs a square and parallel lines and reasons about angles and parallelogram properties, the AI proof never constructs any geometric figure, never discusses angles or parallel lines, and never makes any spatial claim beyond the given setup (C on AB). There are no point position claims, ray orderings, angle decompositions, or inside/outside arguments to check for consistency.
